Antaliepte Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Utena County, Lithuania

Not demolished. Antaliepte's Jewish population numbered 474 (three quarters of the town) in 1897; before WWI, Jews owned 10 shops, with many serving the nearby monastery as grocers, millers, and craftsmen. After WWI, many emigrated to South Africa, the US, South America, and Palestine; by 1931, Jews owned a cloth shop and a heating accessories shop, and the town's only flour mill. Following the German occupation on June 26, 1941, skilled Jews were forced into labor, and on August 26, 1941, all remaining Jews were taken to the Pažiemiai forest and murdered. No information exists about Jews in Antaliepte after the war.
